events.evidenceSummary: Tony's 2024/25 annual FAIR report and the brand's own report-summary article document bean-to-bar cocoa sourcing from Tony's Open Chain partner cooperatives in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, including farmer counts and child-labor monitoring at long-term partner co-ops. The report page renders client-side, so its excerpt is pending verification; the verbatim support comes from the brand's report article.

Barry Callebaut's press release announces the strategic partnership to produce Tony's chocolate from fully traceable cocoa at its Wieze, Belgium plant (fetch blocked; excerpt pending verification). The Invest in Flanders article independently confirms Tony's bars use chocolate 'from the Barry Callebaut plant in Wieze', and the Open Food Facts record lists manufacturing_places: Belgium.

Public customs indexes show recurring Netherlands/Belgium → U.S. ocean shipments with shipper Tony's Chocolonely Nederland B.V. and consignee Tony's Chocolonely Inc. (Panjiva: 259 U.S. shipments updated weekly since 2007; ImportYeti: 130 indexed sea shipments). Search-indexed snapshots of Panjiva's public page show a sample bill of lading from port Rotterdam to the New York/Newark Area, Newark, New Jersey. Full bill-of-lading records sit behind commercial paywalls, so this leg is inferred rather than documented.
events.inferenceBasis: Made-in-Belgium production (Wieze) plus publicly indexed bill-of-lading summaries on ImportYeti and Panjiva showing the Rotterdam → New York/Newark ocean lane to consignee Tony's Chocolonely Inc.; the full customs records behind those summaries are commercially paywalled, so the leg cannot be documented from primary records.
